summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology specializing in embedded systems and real-time firmware development. Experienced in designing and debugging microcontroller-based systems using C/C++, RTOS, and real-time operating systems, with a proven track record of integrating computer vision and robotics control into resource-constrained embedded platforms. Strong hands-on experience with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers for hardware debugging.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback control.
Organized 10+ technical workshops covering Arduino programming, PCB design in EAGLE, and CAD-based mechanical design in SolidWorks.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via real-time Python algorithms.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.
Architected an AI-based real-time chroma keying system for a Mixed Reality headset concept without a green screen.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and collaborative analysis across a distributed team.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency on a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place system with Jetson+Arduino controller and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors.
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 10.9 ms latency) with Arduino C++ servo control and I2C multiplexer for contact-aware grasping; implemented two-link inverse kinematics.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Deployed YOLOv8 real-time object detection on NVIDIA Jetson, sending control commands to STM32 microcontroller over UART with interrupt-driven handling and FreeRTOS task coordination.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 firmware in bare-metal C with timer-triggered ADC conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and low-level I2C driver; achieved 3.68 KB Flash at deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
